name: Maritime

modes.label: Included agent machine
modes.note: Base persistent agent; no runtime time meter. Optional screen pricing not separately published.

modes.label: Computer desktop early access
modes.note: Paid account required; same machine slot economics. Early-access product.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Custom limits, add-on rates and fleet.

features.ip_note: Egress IPs/proxies not documented; CAPTCHAs and logins are handed to a human via request_takeover control links (Computers require a paid plan).

caveats: Storage, snapshot GiB-month and public IPv4 prices are not published in the reviewed sources; null is not free.
The $1/machine headline assumes fully occupied plan slots, not 24×7 concurrency for every retained machine. Base CPU is 1; CLI documents --cpu overrides but no price or public ceiling for 4 CPU.
No active-CPU discount: hosting is flat. Always-on adds $20 even though busy workloads already avoid automatic sleep.
Documentation inconsistency: billing prose says all 3 free agents can run, while pricing and limits tables say 1; use table limit 1 and confirm. Computers are early access and require a paid plan.
Engine base mode cannot price extra retained slots, per-machine RAM/disk add-ons or always-on; do not pool 1-CPU machines into a 4-CPU machine. $5 AI welcome credit is not compute credit.

Plan caps (maritime.sh/docs/limits, checked 2026-09-29): awake-at-once machines Free 1 / Starter 5 / Growth 25 / Scale 60; machines Free 3 / Starter 20 / Growth 100 / Scale 500. Each machine is 1 vCPU / 2 GB / 5 GB SSD; flat add-ons per machine-month: extra RAM $3 / $2.50 / $2 per GB (Starter/Growth/Scale, up to 8 GB), extra SSD $2 / $1.50 / $1 per 5 GB (up to 100 GB), always-on $20; add-ons prorated by day, not available on Free. Workloads needing >60 awake machines or >1 vCPU per machine have no self-serve price (Enterprise is custom).

Billing is a flat monthly plan with no compute-time metering ("There is no metering of messages, tokens, sessions, or compute time", maritime.sh/pricing); the $0 hourly size rate is the encoding of that, the bill is the plan fee.

Students: live /students page and llms.txt give 3 months of Growth free (100 machines, normally $100/mo), code valid on Growth only; the pricing-page FAQ still says 4 months of Starter (stale). Startups: $1,000 credits on acceptance, then $1,000 matched per $1,000 spent up to $5,000 ($10,000 via partner accelerator/fund); credits spend on hosting, LLM usage and add-ons. $5 AI welcome credit (model calls only) expires 30 days after signup.

Plan fee is a flat floor, not usage credit; 'Unused plan capacity doesn't roll over.' Subscription is charged up-front each cycle; extra machine slots stay billed to cycle end even if the agent is deleted. Failed renewal: 14-day grace, then machines are put to sleep (state kept).

Computers are 'a larger machine with a screen, and the screen alone is a paid add-on on an agent' but the Computer's vCPU/RAM and the screen add-on price are unpublished; the computer mode's 1 vCPU/2 GB/5 GB size is an assumption. CLI accepts --cpu (e.g. 1.5 vCPU) with no published price or ceiling.

fleet.verification: Free no card; paid-plan checkout requires card.
fleet.tiers: Free 1 awake agent (3 retained); Starter 5 awake/20 retained; Growth 25/100; Scale 60/500; Enterprise custom.
fleet.notes: Machines include agents and Computers; Free cannot use Computers (0 free computer slots). default 1 is the managed agent machine. 10 agents fit Growth, 50 Scale, 300/1,000 require Enterprise. Upgrades effective immediately. Computers API rate limits: 30 creates, 300 actions and 30 viewer links per minute per key; a wake past the plan's awake-at-once cap returns 429 with a 15 s retry hint; creating machines past the included count is allowed and bills as overflow ($1.50/$1.25/$1.00 per machine-month). A separate 'persisted-computer cap' exists (402 computer_limit, 'ask for a higher cap'), number unpublished.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: On micro-VM hosts the process is snapshotted and resumed, not restarted.
snapshot_auto.note: Trigger: idle timeout (configurable --idle / idleTtlSeconds; Computers sleep after 5 idle minutes or 30 s after close_computer). Memory included: Computers docs say 'After 5 idle minutes the desktop sleeps: memory is snapshotted, open windows and all.' Memory snapshot kept 7 days after last action; after that it wakes from a fresh boot with the same disk. Wake is automatic on chat/trigger/HTTP/file/exec calls (~1.1-1.4 s). Caveat: 'On micro-VM hosts' implies non-microVM hosts restart processes instead.

harness_api.quote: Send a message and wait for the reply. Sleeping agents wake automatically. Pass a conversationId to keep a thread.
harness_api.note: First-party REST (POST /api/agents/{id}/chat with optional conversation_id), CLI (maritime chat) and TS/Python SDKs (agents.chat) deliver prompts to the agent harness running in the VM and return its reply. Templates: Claude Code (Claude Agent SDK; docs: 'Each conversation_id resumes its own Claude Code session'), Codex CLI, OpenClaw, Hermes, ZeroClaw, DeepSeek Harness, or any custom container implementing POST /chat. Request/response only (30 s delivery budget, long tasks reply on next message); no event streaming or conversation-list API documented. Logs streaming exists separately (maritime logs -f).

ingress_rules.quote: Serve a public, no-login web URL for this agent
ingress_rules.note: Public HTTPS URL is opt-in per agent (--public with a chosen --port); otherwise the agent is reached through the authenticated control plane (chat API with mk_ bearer keys, scoped keys) and a per-agent invoke URL that takes an X-Maritime-Webhook-Token (tokenless calls 'being phased out'). Computers' viewer/takeover links are short-lived and bound to one computer and mode. No IP allowlists or auth in front of a public URL (public = no-login).

guest_firewall.quote: Its own dedicated container. On serverless hosts, its own Firecracker microVM with its own guest kernel and a minimal virtio device model
guest_firewall.note: Derived: containers run as root (Claude Code guide) inside a per-agent Firecracker microVM with its own guest kernel, so nftables/iptables should work; not explicitly documented, and whether the container gets CAP_NET_ADMIN is not stated.

secret_proxy.quote: Agents created without a key get a per-agent token for Maritime's OpenAI-format proxy and draw down your prepaid AI credits at provider list price.
secret_proxy.note: Maritime LLM proxy: OPENAI_API_KEY/OPENAI_BASE_URL point at Maritime's metered proxy with a per-agent token (Codex docs: 'With no key set, Maritime injects a per-agent proxy token.'); covers model calls only (OpenAI-format / Responses API; Claude Code needs its own ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, 'no proxy fallback'). All other secrets (including your own LLM keys) are AES-256-GCM encrypted env vars injected into the VM, so they are visible inside it. No arbitrary-HTTP or non-HTTP credential injection.

volume_attach.quote: A persistent volume, mounted at /data for most templates. This is the agent's memory: it survives restarts, redeploys, and sleep/wake. Everything outside it is disposable.
volume_attach.note: Each machine has exactly one persistent volume (/data), sized 5 GB base up to 100 GB via the flat Extra SSD add-on ($2/$1.50/$1 per 5 GB-month). That is the machine's own persistent disk, not an extra attachable volume; no API to create/attach additional volumes.

volume_shared.quote: Its own persistent volume, with no shared filesystem between agents
volume_shared.note: Deliberately no shared filesystem between agents (official Maritime blog). File transfer is via the Files API (100 MB per file).

docker_inside.quote: Its own dedicated container. On serverless hosts, its own Firecracker microVM with its own guest kernel and a minimal virtio device model
docker_inside.note: derived: an agent is one container process in a Firecracker microVM; no docs describe a docker daemon or nested containers running inside that guest

nested_virt.quote: Its own dedicated container. On serverless hosts, its own Firecracker microVM with its own guest kernel and a minimal virtio device model
nested_virt.note: derived: single-process container inside a microVM guest; /dev/kvm passthrough for nested VMs/emulators is not documented

anti_bot.quote: If you reach a login, CAPTCHA or payment step, call request_takeover with a short reason and show the user the link it returns
anti_bot.note: not offered: CAPTCHAs/logins are escalated to a human via takeover links rather than solved by stealth/fingerprint evasion; no anti-bot feature documented

ssh.quote: Run a one-shot, non-interactive shell command in the agent's VM (its sandboxed container). Wakes a sleeping agent.
ssh.note: not offered: the documented ways into a running agent are chat, the exec API/CLI (one-shot commands), and file APIs; no SSH access, key, or port is documented anywhere (CLI reference, API reference)

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Template capture	Usually 1 to 10 minutes (snapshots the image and volume)
snapshot_on_demand.note: Packaging a running agent into a Template snapshots its image and volume on demand (dashboard-triggered); no separate lower-level 'checkpoint now' CLI/API verb is documented

fork.quote: Templates are also how you share. Package any working agent (image, config, memory) into a template others can clone: see Templates.
fork.note: an existing agent can be packaged as a Template and cloned into new independent agents

fork_running.quote: Template capture	Usually 1 to 10 minutes (snapshots the image and volume)
fork_running.note: derived: template capture takes 1-10 minutes and its interaction with a currently-running agent is not documented; no claim that cloning happens without pausing/affecting the source agent

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: A persistent volume, mounted at /data for most templates. This is the agent's memory: it survives restarts, redeploys, and sleep/wake.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: derived: Maritime's docs use 'memory' to mean the persistent /data volume, not live process/RAM state; template clones start a fresh container from that data, not a running-process fork

live_resize.quote: Agents that need more can be sized up to 8 GB RAM and 100 GB SSD at creation or later from the agent's settings, at flat monthly add-on prices
live_resize.note: no CLI/API 'resize' verb is documented and env/config changes explicitly note they 'apply on the agent's next boot unless you push them into the running container with --reload'; resource resizing is not shown to apply without a restart

own_agent_api.quote: A persistent Linux desktop (XFCE, Chromium, LibreOffice) for each of your end users, driven by your model.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Maritime hosts YOUR agent/model driving the desktop or chat; it does not offer its own first-party browser/computer-use/research agent that customers call as a black box

lang_python.quote: Hermes	hermes	Python	A self-improving agent with persistent memory and its own full dashboard
lang_python.note: Hermes template runtime is Python; custom Docker images can also ship any Python runtime

lang_node.quote: Claude Code	claude_code	Node.js (Claude Agent SDK)	... Codex	codex	Node.js (Codex CLI) ... OpenClaw	openclaw	Node.js
lang_node.note: Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw and DeepSeek Harness templates all run on Node.js; the CLI itself requires Node.js 20.12+

public_ipv4.quote: Any repo with a Dockerfile can be served on a public, no-login HTTPS URL.
public_ipv4.note: not offered: machines are reached through HTTPS invoke/public URLs and a chat/webhook API, not a per-machine public IPv4 address; no IPv4 allocation is documented

egress_allowlist.quote: No key: the Maritime LLM proxy. ... Your own key: direct. Set OPENAI_API_KEY ... and the agent talks to the provider directly
egress_allowlist.note: not offered: the only outbound control documented is an optional LLM-call proxy for model traffic; no allow/deny list, no-internet mode, or security-group-style egress control is documented

egress_http_rules.quote: No key: the Maritime LLM proxy. ... Your own key: direct.
egress_http_rules.note: not offered: no method/path-level egress rule feature is documented anywhere in the docs; only the model-call proxy is mentioned

gpu.quote: EVERY AGENT	VCPU 1	RAM 2 GB	SSD 5 GB	WAKE ~1s
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Every plan/size in the pricing and limits pages lists only vCPU/RAM/SSD; no GPU machine or GPU add-on exists

windows.quote: On serverless hosts, its own Firecracker microVM with its own guest kernel
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Firecracker microVMs run Linux guest kernels; every template, Computer desktop (XFCE/Chromium) and doc is Linux-only

macos.quote: An agent is a long-lived program running in its own isolated VM (a sandboxed container)
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; a Linux Firecracker-microVM hosting product, no Apple hardware/macOS VM is offered

arm64.note: not documented: no architecture choice (x86_64 vs arm64) appears anywhere in pricing, CLI, or API docs; treated as not offered

self_host.quote: Host persistent agents on the cloud. Each one in its own VM.
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Maritime is a hosted SaaS platform; there is no self-hosted/on-prem distribution of the platform itself (only client SDK/CLI code is open on GitHub)

byoc.quote: Host persistent agents on the cloud. Each one in its own VM.
byoc.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; no bring-your-own-cloud deployment option is documented, including on the Enterprise tier

open_source.quote: maritime-sdk: Official TypeScript + Python SDKs for Maritime — provision and drive AI agents from your own backend (MIT)
open_source.note: the client SDK and CLI are MIT-licensed on GitHub, but the core hosting platform/runtime is closed-source; no repo for the platform itself

soc2.quote: Enterprise support is dedicated, with terms set in your agreement.
soc2.note: not offered: no SOC 2 attestation, trust page, or compliance page exists anywhere on maritime.sh (checked pricing, docs, blog); Enterprise terms are only 'set in your agreement'

hipaa.quote: Enterprise support is dedicated, with terms set in your agreement.
hipaa.note: not offered/not documented: no HIPAA or BAA mention anywhere on the site

sso.quote: Sign in with Google or GitHub? You have no password, so use the browser flow, or paste a token from maritime.sh/cli/auth
sso.note: account login supports Google/GitHub OAuth for individual users, but no SAML/OIDC enterprise SSO is documented anywhere

eu_data_residency.quote: the network round-trip, which is tens of milliseconds in Europe and under 200 ms from most of the world
eu_data_residency.note: not documented: no region selection appears in the CLI, API, or pricing docs (single implicit deployment), so there is no way to pin machines/data to an EU region

max_session_h.quote: Always-on is for agents that must react in milliseconds, around the clock; everything else sleeps when idle at no cost.
max_session_h.note: no maximum runtime/session length is documented; an always-on agent (or one kept awake by continuous requests) runs indefinitely. The only caps are on how many machines may be awake at once, not how long any one machine may run
